seo.description: Learn whether to sell your diamond and setting together or separately by comparing diamond value, gold or platinum, removal costs and net offers.

title: Where to Sell a Diamond in Belgium: Antwerp and Online Options
excerpt: Belgium offers several ways to sell a diamond, from specialist buyers in Antwerp to online valuation services. Learn how the options differ, how to verify a buyer and what to prepare before requesting an offer.
content_html:
If you want to sell a diamond in Belgium, you can approach a specialist diamond buyer, a jeweller, an auction house, a consignment business or an online buyer. The right choice depends on what you are selling and whether your priority is speed, convenience, specialist expertise or broader market exposure.

Antwerp is a natural place to begin because of its long-established diamond district and concentration of professional diamond businesses. However, an Antwerp address does not automatically guarantee a strong offer or transparent service. The individual buyer, valuation method and written terms still need to be checked.

The direct answer is:

For most private sellers, a specialist diamond buyer who offers an initial online review and a verifiable physical assessment in Antwerp provides a practical balance of expertise, privacy and speed.

Sothis Diamonds offers online submissions and private appointments from its Antwerp location. You can request a free, no-obligation diamond valuation using photographs and any available certificate.

Why Sell a Diamond in Antwerp?

Antwerp has participated in the international diamond trade for centuries. Its diamond district remains home to a concentrated network of diamond companies, trading organisations and supporting services.

For a private seller, the practical advantage is access to professionals who regularly handle loose diamonds and diamond jewellery. A specialist may be better equipped than a general precious-metal buyer to evaluate origin, carat weight, colour, clarity, cut, shape, grading reports and current diamond demand.

Antwerp’s reputation does not mean every business offers the same service. Some companies operate only within the trade, some sell jewellery without purchasing from the public and others may focus on specific categories of diamonds.

Before travelling to the district, confirm that the business buys from private individuals, handles your type of item and offers appointments at a verifiable address.

Your Main Diamond-Selling Options in Belgium

The best route depends on whether you have a standard certified diamond, an antique jewel, a branded piece, a laboratory-grown diamond or an exceptional stone that may benefit from auction exposure.

A direct buyer may be suitable when you want a clear offer without waiting for a future retail customer. Auction and consignment can make sense for rare jewellery, but the advertised sale price is not the amount the seller necessarily receives after commissions and other charges.

Specialist Diamond Buyer in Antwerp

A specialist buyer should be able to explain what is driving the offer.

For a loose diamond, this normally includes natural or laboratory-grown origin, weight, colour, clarity, cut, shape, proportions, fluorescence, condition, grading report and current demand. For jewellery, the buyer should also consider the setting, smaller stones, precious metal, brand and craftsmanship.

The process often starts online. You submit photographs, specifications and documents, after which the buyer determines whether the item fits its current purchasing criteria. If it does, a physical inspection can be arranged.

A preliminary online estimate should not be treated as an unconditional final price. Photographs cannot confirm exact weight, origin, treatments, hidden damage or whether a stone matches its grading report. The important point is that the buyer explains what will be checked and what could cause the amount to change.

Selling Through a Belgian Jeweller

Some jewellers buy pre-owned diamonds, while others offer only trade-in, store credit or consignment.

A trade-in can be useful when you intend to purchase another item, but its headline allowance should be compared with the price of the replacement jewellery. A large trade-in figure does not necessarily create the strongest overall financial result if the new purchase is priced differently.

Consignment allows the jeweller to offer your item to a retail customer and pay you after it sells. This can create broader exposure, but there is no guaranteed completion date.

Before leaving a diamond with a jeweller, obtain a written intake document. It should describe the item, report number, agreed asking price or reserve, fees, insurance responsibility, payment timing and return procedure.

When an Auction House May Be Appropriate

An auction can be suitable for important fancy-coloured diamonds, signed jewellery, historic pieces, exceptional large stones or items with recognised provenance.

The auction house will normally assess whether the item fits an upcoming sale and may recommend an estimate and reserve. The result then depends on bidder interest.

Ask for the complete seller-cost schedule before consigning. Commission, photography, insurance, transport, authentication, unsold-item and withdrawal charges can affect the amount you ultimately receive. Terms differ between auction businesses and can change, so use the current written agreement rather than an old fee example.

An ordinary commercial diamond may not benefit from the additional time and uncertainty of auction. Compare the expected net auction proceeds with a genuine direct offer.

Can You Sell a Diamond Online from Belgium?

Yes. An online valuation allows sellers in Brussels, Ghent, Bruges, Liège, Leuven and elsewhere in Belgium to begin without travelling immediately.

You can submit clear photographs of the diamond or complete jewellery, together with the grading report, invoice or previous appraisal. The buyer can then advise whether an appointment or secure physical handover is worthwhile.

Online submission is particularly useful when you are uncertain whether the item fits a buyer’s criteria. It can prevent unnecessary travel while allowing you to ask about the process, likely documentation and inspection requirements.

If shipping becomes necessary, confirm the exact instructions, tracking, insurance or liability coverage and return procedure in writing. Ordinary parcel services may exclude jewellery, loose stones or high-value contents even when a shipping label permits a declared value.

Read How to Sell a Diamond Online Safely from Belgium or Europe before sending an item.

How to Verify a Diamond Buyer in Belgium

Begin by checking whether the business is legally identifiable.

Belgium’s Crossroads Bank for Enterprises provides a free Public Search containing information about registered entities and establishment units. Compare the enterprise name, number, status and address with the information shown on the buyer’s website and written offer.

A registration entry confirms that an entity is recorded; it does not prove that every offer will be fair. You should also examine the buyer’s physical contact details, professional history, independent reviews and written terms.

Contact the business through the telephone number or email published on its official website. Be cautious if someone approaches you through a messaging app and then asks you to send the diamond to a different person, address or bank account.

A trustworthy process should make it clear:

  • Whether the initial amount is an estimate or a confirmed offer
  • What physical tests will be performed
  • Whether any valuation, removal or shipping fee applies
  • Who is responsible for the item during transport and inspection
  • How and when payment is made
  • What happens if you decline the final offer

Do not rely on a payment screenshot. Confirm independently that cleared funds have reached your account before treating the transaction as complete.

What Happens During a Diamond Valuation in Antwerp?

A market valuation begins by identifying the diamond and reviewing its documents.

If the stone has a GIA, IGI, HRD Antwerp or other grading report, the buyer can check its recorded specifications and report number. The physical diamond may then be weighed, measured and tested to confirm that its origin and characteristics correspond with the document.

For a mounted diamond, the setting may prevent exact weighing or complete observation. The buyer may initially estimate certain characteristics and decide whether professional removal is justified.

Condition is also important. Chips, abrasion, recutting potential and wear around the setting can affect marketability.

Once the relevant details have been confirmed, the buyer considers current demand and the costs associated with purchasing, holding and remarketing the item. The resulting offer is a market purchase figure—not an insurance replacement appraisal.

What Documents Should You Bring?

Bring the diamond grading report if one exists. A complete report or clear PDF is more useful than a handwritten list of grades.

Invoices, insurance appraisals, brand certificates, original packaging and repair records may help identify the item and support provenance. They do not guarantee that the original price or appraisal amount will be recovered.

You may also be asked for valid identification and information showing that you are authorised to sell the property. Exact compliance requirements depend on the transaction and business, so confirm them before the appointment.

Inherited jewellery can often be reviewed without its original diamond certificate. Preserve any document, photograph or box connected with the item and explain what is known about its history.

For additional guidance, read What Documents Do You Need to Sell a Diamond?.

How to Compare Diamond Offers in Belgium

Compare offers on the same basis.

Confirm whether each amount covers the entire jewellery item or only its centre diamond. One buyer may include the gold, platinum and side stones, while another intends to remove the main diamond and return the setting.

Ask whether the offer is subject to inspection, whether fees will be deducted and what payment method will be used. An offer that appears higher can produce a lower net payout after commission, shipping or return costs.

Written explanations are especially useful when two offers differ significantly. The difference may come from grading assumptions, diamond origin, hidden condition issues, selling method or the buyer’s current inventory needs.

A genuine offer that the buyer is prepared to complete is more useful than an optimistic online calculator result or an uncompleted marketplace listing.

Preparing for an Antwerp Appointment

Do not remove a diamond from its ring or pay for a new grading report before receiving initial advice. The complete jewellery may have value through its setting, smaller stones, brand or period design.

Take photographs before travelling and keep the item in a secure jewellery box or pouch. Do not display valuable jewellery unnecessarily in public areas.

Confirm the appointment, exact office address and name of the person you are meeting through the business’s official contact channel. Ask what identification and documents are required.

Sothis Diamonds is located in Antwerp’s diamond district at Hoveniersstraat 2, Bus 210, 2018 Antwerpen. Confirm your appointment before visiting.

Three Illustrative Selling Situations

A seller in Brussels has a certified one-carat natural diamond ring. An online review confirms that the item may fit the buyer’s criteria, so the seller arranges an Antwerp appointment. The diamond and report are verified before a written offer is provided.

A second seller owns an unsigned inherited ring without paperwork. Photographs are sufficient for an initial conversation, but the final assessment requires physical testing of the mounted diamond and precious metal.

A third seller has a signed antique necklace. A direct diamond offer alone may overlook the maker, design and provenance, so the complete jewellery should be considered before choosing between a specialist sale, auction or consignment.

These examples show why the right Belgian selling route depends on the item rather than the seller’s location alone.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where can I sell diamonds in Belgium?

You can approach a specialist diamond buyer, jeweller, auction house, consignment business or online buyer. The strongest option depends on the diamond and your priorities.

Is Antwerp the best place to sell a diamond?

Antwerp offers access to a concentrated professional diamond market, but location alone does not guarantee the best offer. Verify and compare individual buyers.

Can private individuals sell diamonds in Antwerp?

Yes, but not every company in the diamond district buys from the public. Confirm its services and arrange an appointment before travelling.

Can I request a diamond valuation in Antwerp without selling?

Yes. A no-obligation valuation allows you to understand the current offer before deciding whether to proceed.

Can I sell a diamond online from another Belgian city?

Yes. Begin with photographs and documents. Physical inspection can follow through an Antwerp appointment or an agreed secure transport process.

Do I need a diamond certificate?

Not always. A diamond can still be tested and assessed without its original report, although additional uncertainty may affect the process.

Can I sell inherited diamond jewellery in Belgium?

Potentially. Keep all available documents and ensure that you have authority to sell the inherited property.

Can I sell a laboratory-grown diamond in Belgium?

It can be submitted for review, but laboratory-grown diamonds have a different and generally more selective resale market.

Should I visit several Antwerp buyers?

Comparing written offers can be useful, provided they cover the same item, fees and payment terms.

Will an Antwerp buyer pay the insurance appraisal amount?

Usually not. Insurance appraisals address replacement requirements, while a resale offer reflects the current secondary market.

Is shipping a diamond within Belgium automatically insured?

No. Carrier acceptance and declared value do not always mean jewellery is covered. Obtain written confirmation of the applicable liability or insurance arrangement.

How do I verify a Belgian diamond business?

Check its details through the Belgian Crossroads Bank for Enterprises Public Search and compare them with its official website, address and written documents.

How quickly will I receive payment?

Timing depends on inspection, acceptance and the agreed payment method. Confirm the expected payment schedule in writing before transferring ownership.

Where Should You Sell Your Diamond in Belgium?

For an ordinary loose diamond or diamond ring, a specialist buyer offering both online review and physical assessment in Antwerp can provide a direct and convenient route.

Auction or consignment may be more suitable for an exceptional, signed or historically important item. A jeweller may be useful for trade-in, while a general gold buyer should not be assumed to provide a complete diamond assessment.

Whichever option you choose, verify the business, understand whether the initial figure is conditional and compare the final net amount rather than the headline offer.

Request a free, private diamond valuation from Sothis Diamonds in Antwerp.

title: How to Sell to an Antwerp Diamond Buyer from Anywhere in Europe
content_html:
You do not need to live in Belgium—or travel with a valuable stone—to approach a professional diamond buyer in Antwerp. A secure remote process can begin with documents, photographs and a preliminary assessment, followed by insured delivery or an in-person appointment for final inspection.

If you want to sell a diamond to Antwerp from Europe, the safest route is a staged transaction. First, provide enough information for an indicative valuation. Next, verify the buyer and agree in writing how the stone will be transported, inspected, priced, paid for or returned. Only then should the diamond leave your possession.

This guide explains that process for sellers in the European Union, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Norway and other European countries outside the EU customs territory.

Why Sellers Look to Antwerp

Antwerp has a long-established professional diamond market, with specialist expertise in natural stones, grading, recutting and resale. That concentration of buyers can be useful when a standard jewellery shop is not the right outlet for a certified diamond, an inherited stone, an engagement ring or a higher-value piece.

The city’s reputation does not remove the need for due diligence. In Belgium, businesses that buy and sell unmounted diamonds must meet registration requirements. Registered diamond traders are also subject to anti-money-laundering controls, including customer identification and specific measures for remote transactions.

A seller should therefore expect reasonable identity and provenance questions rather than treating them as a warning sign.

Can You Sell a Diamond to Antwerp Without Travelling?

Yes. A remote diamond valuation in Europe can give you an initial indication before you decide whether to send the item or arrange an appointment. However, a responsible buyer will normally distinguish between a preliminary estimate and a binding offer.

Photographs and certificates can reveal useful information, but they cannot show every factor that affects resale value. The buyer may need to:

  • Confirm that the stone matches its grading report
  • Test whether it is natural or laboratory-grown
  • Check for damage or treatments
  • Assess fluorescence and proportions
  • Inspect the condition of the setting

The final price should follow a physical examination by a qualified professional.

How to Sell to an Antwerp Diamond Buyer: The Six-Step Process

Step 1: Send the Essential Details

Begin with clear photographs of the complete item and the stone from several angles. Include the grading report number and a scan or photograph of the report if one exists.

You should also state:

  • Whether the stone is loose or mounted
  • Whether it is natural or laboratory-grown, to the best of your knowledge
  • Its approximate carat weight
  • Whether you have an invoice, valuation or repair record
  • Whether the item was inherited

Do not edit photographs in a way that changes the colour or hides signs of wear. Accurate information makes the initial assessment more useful and reduces the chance of a significant revision after inspection.

Step 2: Receive a Preliminary Valuation

The buyer can review the reported carat weight, cut, colour, clarity, shape, certification, condition and current resale demand.

Ask whether the figure provided is:

  • A broad valuation range
  • A preliminary estimate
  • A conditional purchase offer
  • A firm offer

At this stage, it will usually be provisional.

A trustworthy online diamond buyer in Antwerp should explain what assumptions the estimate uses and what could cause the final offer to change. Be cautious if a remote quote is presented as guaranteed before the stone has been authenticated and inspected.

Step 3: Verify the Buyer and Agree to the Terms

Before sending a valuable item, confirm the buyer’s:

  • Legal business name
  • Physical address
  • Contact details
  • Company registration
  • Diamond-trader registration, where applicable
  • Written purchase and return terms

Belgium’s FPS Economy provides a public Diamond Supervision register that can be used to check registered diamond companies.

You should also check independent reviews and confirm how complaints, rejected offers and returns are handled.

Request written answers to four important questions:

  1. Who bears the risk while the diamond is being transported?
  2. What level of insurance applies?
  3. When does ownership of the diamond transfer?
  4. Who pays the return costs if you decline the final offer?

Do not rely on a telephone promise for any of these points.

Step 4: Use an Agreed, Insured Delivery Method

Use only the delivery method approved in writing by the buyer. Confirm that the insurance specifically covers jewellery or loose diamonds for the declared value.

Many ordinary postal and parcel services restrict or exclude precious stones, particularly above modest value limits. A tracking number alone does not mean the item is insured.

When packaging the diamond:

  • Follow the buyer’s and carrier’s instructions
  • Package the item discreetly
  • Keep photographs of the item and sealed parcel
  • Retain every shipping receipt
  • Record the tracking and insurance information
  • Avoid writing “diamond” or “jewellery” on the outside of the parcel unless required by the specialist carrier

Do not send the item until you have written confirmation of the insurance coverage and responsibility for transport risk.

Step 5: Let the Buyer Authenticate and Inspect the Item

After secure receipt, the buyer should verify that the item matches the information supplied.

For a mounted diamond, the setting may limit the precision of the weight, colour and clarity assessment. The buyer may suggest removing the stone from its setting, but this should never happen without your prior approval.

Following inspection, request the final offer in writing. It should:

  • Identify the item being purchased
  • State the final amount
  • Confirm the payment currency
  • Explain any fees or deductions
  • Include an acceptance period
  • Explain the return process if you decline

If the final price differs materially from the preliminary valuation, request a specific explanation instead of feeling pressured to decide immediately.

Step 6: Accept the Offer or Arrange the Return

If you accept the offer, complete the buyer’s identity and ownership checks and confirm the payment method.

A traceable bank transfer is generally easier to document than a cash payment. Check when the payment will be released and when it should reach your account, especially when converting between euros, pounds or Swiss francs.

If you decline the offer, follow the agreed return process. Confirm the delivery address, declared insurance value and tracking details before the item is dispatched back to you.

What Determines the Price of Your Diamond?

The familiar four Cs—carat, cut, colour and clarity—matter, but they do not determine a cash resale offer by themselves.

Other important factors include:

  • Diamond shape
  • Grading laboratory
  • Fluorescence
  • Proportions
  • Condition
  • Treatments
  • Natural or laboratory-grown origin
  • Current demand for that specification
  • The buyer’s expected resale route
  • Whether the stone may require recutting

A jewellery insurance valuation is not the same as a buying offer. Insurance documents often estimate the cost of replacing the item at retail. A buyer must consider authentication, handling, potential recutting, inventory time and the price available in the secondary market.

Certification can help because it gives the buyer an independent description of the stone. However, a missing grading report does not automatically make a sale impossible.

The buyer may offer testing or laboratory grading, sometimes at a cost. Agree to any charge before work begins.

Selling From an EU Country

If the diamond is moving from one EU Member State to Belgium, the EU customs union means that customs duties are not charged simply because goods cross an internal EU border.

This makes it easier to sell a diamond across Europe within the EU. However, it does not remove:

  • Carrier restrictions
  • Insurance requirements
  • Buyer identification checks
  • Payment verification
  • Possible tax consequences in your home country

Keep evidence of the item’s origin and your transaction, including:

  • Purchase invoice or inheritance record
  • Grading report
  • Photographs
  • Shipping receipt
  • Buyer correspondence
  • Final written offer
  • Bank payment record

Local rules concerning gains, inherited property or repeated commercial activity differ. Obtain country-specific tax advice when the value is significant.

Selling From the UK, Switzerland, Norway or Another Non-EU Country

Geographically European does not always mean inside the EU customs territory.

Sending a diamond from a non-EU country to Belgium may require:

  • Export and import declarations
  • An accurate value and description
  • Customs documentation
  • Coordination over duties or VAT
  • Brokerage arrangements
  • Temporary admission if the item is being sent only for inspection

Do not mark a commercial sale as a gift or deliberately understate its value.

Before shipping, ask the buyer and carrier for the exact paperwork. You should also obtain written confirmation of who will be the importer of record and who will be responsible for charges if you do not accept the offer.

What to Prepare Before Requesting a Valuation

Clear Images

Photograph the complete item, the front and back of the stone, the setting, hallmarks and any visible wear.

Grading Information

Provide the grading laboratory’s name, report number, report date and a copy of the complete report if available.

Ownership and Provenance

Keep the invoice, inheritance paperwork, insurance schedule or another record showing how you acquired the item.

Identification

A regulated buyer may ask for a passport or national identity card and proof of address, especially during a remote transaction.

Payment Details

Use an account in the seller’s name. Confirm currency-conversion costs before accepting an offer in a different currency.

How to Choose a Safe Antwerp Diamond Buyer

Look for a buyer who:

  • Gives you time to review the written terms
  • Separates the initial estimate from the final offer
  • Explains the inspection process
  • Uses traceable communication
  • Clearly allocates shipping and insurance responsibility
  • Provides a verifiable physical address
  • Offers a written return procedure
  • Does not pressure you into making an immediate decision

Verify claims of Belgian diamond-trader registration through the official FPS Economy search rather than relying only on a logo displayed on a website.

Confirm the address independently and call a published business number before sending the parcel.

Be cautious if a buyer:

  • Pressures you to ship immediately
  • Demands unexplained upfront fees
  • Requests payment to release your proceeds
  • Instructs you to misdescribe the parcel
  • Changes the bank account or delivery address at the last minute
  • Refuses to explain the return process
  • Will not provide the offer in writing

If anything changes during the transaction, pause and verify the new information through a second contact channel.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

The biggest mistake is treating the highest online estimate as the best offer without comparing its assumptions and terms.

A generous headline figure has little value if it:

  • Depends on an unrealistic diamond grade
  • Excludes important fees
  • Is reduced without explanation after inspection
  • Requires uninsured shipping
  • Does not include a clear return process

Other avoidable mistakes include sending original documents without keeping copies, allowing a mounted stone to be removed without consent, confusing an insurance appraisal with resale value and failing to agree on return arrangements in advance.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I Have to Visit Antwerp to Sell My Diamond?

No. The process can begin online from most European countries. You may complete the sale remotely if secure transport, identity checks, inspection and payment are agreed upon.

For exceptional stones—or if you prefer face-to-face verification—an appointment may still be sensible.

Is an Online Diamond Valuation Final?

Usually not. It is generally an indication based on the information you provide. A final offer should follow physical authentication and condition assessment.

Can I Sell a Diamond Ring Rather Than a Loose Stone?

Yes. Many buyers assess rings and other diamond jewellery.

The buyer should explain whether the offer covers the complete piece, the centre stone alone or separate values for the diamond, setting and precious metal.

Do I Pay Customs Duty When Sending a Diamond to Belgium?

For goods moving between EU Member States, no customs duty is levied at internal EU borders.

Shipments from outside the EU customs territory can require declarations and may create tax, VAT or brokerage obligations. Check the exact route before dispatching the item.

Can I Sell a Diamond Without a Certificate?

Potentially, yes. A certificate can make the initial assessment more precise, but a qualified buyer can inspect an uncertified stone.

Ask in advance whether testing, unsetting or laboratory grading will be required and who will pay for it.

How Quickly Will I Be Paid?

Payment timelines vary. Ask for the expected inspection period and payment schedule in writing before shipping.

Allow additional time for weekends, compliance checks, international bank transfers and currency conversion.

Start With a Secure Preliminary Valuation

Ready to understand what your diamond may be worth in Antwerp?

Request a confidential preliminary valuation using clear photographs, any available grading report and your country of residence. Before sending the item, confirm the final inspection, insured-delivery, payment and return terms in writing.
